recent_posts.title: Pretext vs. Traditional Layout in 2026: Is the DOM Finally Obsolete?
recent_posts.summary: Pretext is a pure JavaScript text measurement library by Cheng Lou that performs layout calculations outside the browser's main rendering cycle, eliminating DOM reflows. It claims sub-millisecond layout performance and full i18n support. A community showcase called the Pretext Wall demonstrates complex typographic effects like text flow around obstacles, shrink-wrap chat bubbles, and live line-by-line layout that would be impractical with traditional DOM-based rendering.

recent_posts.title: The Blue Board and the Behemoth: Why Qualcomm Just Bought Arduino
recent_posts.summary: Qualcomm has quietly acquired Arduino, the open-source hardware platform used by millions of hobbyists, students, and engineers worldwide. The acquisition raises questions about the future of Arduino's open-source ethos and accessibility — particularly for developers in emerging markets who rely on cheap clones. The piece explores the history of Arduino, the implications of a billion-dollar chip company owning the platform, and what corporate acquisitions typically mean for open-source communities.

recent_posts.title: Why Consoles Are Slowly Turning Into PCs?
recent_posts.summary: Gaming consoles are converging with PC architecture, using the same x86 CPUs and AMD GPUs. PlayStation and Xbox exclusives are increasingly releasing on PC, while Valve's Steam Deck blurs the hardware distinction further. This shift raises questions about what differentiates consoles from PCs beyond convenience, and whether traditional console makers can maintain their identity as the hardware gap narrows.

recent_posts.title: Who Owns Art in the Age of AI?
recent_posts.summary: Explores the philosophical and ethical questions surrounding AI-generated art, particularly in light of the 2025 Ghibli-style AI trend. Examines competing perspectives on whether AI art constitutes genuine artistic creation, questions around authorship and value when machines can replicate human artistic styles, and whether AI represents a threat to traditional art or an evolution of creative expression.

recent_posts.title: The Silent Company powering Apple, NVIDIA and (maybe) WW3
recent_posts.summary: TSMC manufactures the most advanced semiconductors at unmatched scale and precision, powering everything from smartphones and AI infrastructure to medical equipment and military hardware. The company operates invisibly behind major tech brands like Apple and NVIDIA, yet sits at the center of geopolitical tensions between the US and China. Understanding TSMC's foundry business model reveals how modern technology supply chains actually work and why this single manufacturer has become critical infrastructure for the global digital economy.

recent_posts.title: Pig-Butchering Scams Aren’t Small-Time Anymore
recent_posts.summary: Pig-butchering scams have evolved from small-time operations into sophisticated, organized criminal networks, as evidenced by the recent arrest of billionaire Chen Zhi in China. These scams build trust over weeks or months through fake relationships on platforms like WhatsApp, Instagram, and Telegram before defrauding victims. Unlike traditional scams, they don't rely on urgency or obvious red flags, making them effective even against tech-savvy professionals and CEOs. The problem is particularly severe in developing countries where weak financial regulation and cryptocurrency's legal ambiguity make recovery nearly impossible once funds are stolen.

recent_posts.title: Why PC Gaming in Pakistan Is Bigger Than Ever
recent_posts.summary: PC gaming in Pakistan has improved dramatically due to better internet infrastructure from providers like Nayatel and Stormfiber, more affordable game pricing through sales and free-to-play titles, and optimized hardware that lasts longer. The growth of esports and content creation is also establishing gaming as a viable career path in the country.

recent_posts.title: How Cameras and Lasers Are Fighting to Drive Your Car
recent_posts.summary: Self-driving cars use two competing approaches for environmental perception: LiDAR systems that use lasers for 3D mapping versus camera-based computer vision with AI. This fundamental technology choice has driven billions in investment and created vastly different vehicle designs and costs. Companies like Waymo use expensive LiDAR hardware while Tesla relies solely on cameras and vision algorithms, arguing that human-like visual perception is sufficient for autonomous driving.

recent_posts.title: Bluetooth Explained: The Tech Behind Your Wireless Experience
recent_posts.summary: Bluetooth technology powers everyday wireless devices like headphones, keyboards, and car audio systems. Understanding its versions, power modes, range-speed-battery tradeoffs, and vendor customizations from companies like Apple and Google helps explain common connectivity issues. The technology continues evolving with features like Auracast and precise tracking.
